items.title: Warning: Humans cannot reliably detect speech deepfakes

judge.evidence_empirical: We presented genuine and deepfake audio to n = 529 individuals and asked them to identify the deepfakes.
judge.evidence_topic: Speech deepfakes are artificial voices generated by machine learning models.
judge.reason: The main finding matches the abstract: 'Listeners only correctly spotted the deepfakes 73% of the time'.

items.title: Cortical-striatal brain network distinguishes deepfake from real speaker identity

judge.evidence_empirical: During an identity matching task, participants show intermediate performance with deepfake voices, indicating levels of deception and resistance to deepfake identity spoofing.
judge.evidence_topic: Here, we test the neurocognitive sensitivity of 25 participants to accept or reject person identities as recreated in audio deepfakes.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga a percepção humana de áudios deepfake, incluindo 25 participantes em uma tarefa de correspondência de identidade com medidas cerebrais (fMRI). O estudo é empírico, os dados extraídos estão corretos, e o achado principal está totalmente apoiado pelo resumo (parcialmente enganados; rede cortical-estriatal distingue).

items.title: Deepfake detection with and without content warnings

judge.evidence_empirical: We conduct an experiment to measure people's alertness to and ability to detect a high-quality deepfake among a set of videos.
judge.evidence_topic: We conduct an experiment to measure people's alertness to and ability to detect a high-quality deepfake among a set of videos.
judge.reason: O artigo relata um experimento com participantes humanos sobre detecção de deepfakes, com metodologia adequada, e o achado extraído é fiel ao resumo.

items.title: Voice clones sound realistic but not (yet) hyperrealistic

judge.evidence_empirical: We investigated the extent to which AI-generated voices sound real to human listeners, and whether listeners can accurately distinguish between human and AI-generated voices.
judge.evidence_topic: AI-generated voices are increasingly prevalent in our lives, via virtual assistants, automated customer service, and voice-overs. With increased availability and affordability of AI-generated voices, we need to examine how humans perceive them.
judge.reason: O resumo indica que o estudo investiga a percepção de vozes geradas por IA (clones e vozes do espaço latente) por ouvintes humanos, medindo realismo percebido, capacidade de distinção e atributos sociais. O método extraído (avaliações de realismo, distinção, confiabilidade e dominância) coincide com o descrito. O achado principal extraído ('Clones de voz soam tão reais quanto vozes humanas, mas sem efeito de hiper-realismo. Vozes de IA foram julgadas mais dominantes e algumas mais confiáveis.') é diretamente suportado pelo trecho 'We find that voice clones can sound as real as human voices, making it difficult for listeners to distinguish between them. However, we did not observe a hyperrealism effect. Both types of AI-generated voices were evaluated as more dominant than human voices, with some AI-generated voices also being perceived as more trustworthy.' Portanto, todos os critérios são atendidos.

items.title: AI-synthesized faces are indistinguishable from real faces and more trustworthy

judge.evidence_empirical: Our evaluation of the photorealism of AI-synthesized faces indicates that synthesis engines have passed through the uncanny valley and are capable of creating faces that are indistinguishable-and more trustworthy-than real faces.
judge.evidence_topic: AI-synthesized text, audio, image, and video are being weaponized... Our evaluation of the photorealism of AI-synthesized faces indicates... are indistinguishable-and more trustworthy-than real faces.
judge.reason: All criteria met. Abstract clearly reports empirical evaluation of human perception of synthetic faces.

items.title: What you see is not what you get anymore: a mixed-methods approach on human perception of AI-generated images

judge.evidence_empirical: A total of 104 participants took part in an online survey, classifying 50 images (25 real, 25 AI-generated)
judge.evidence_topic: This study explores human perception and detection capabilities regarding AI-generated images of landscapes, architecture, and interiors
judge.reason: O artigo investiga a percepção humana de imagens sintéticas geradas por IA, dentro do escopo do pedido. O estudo é empírico, com 104 participantes em survey online, e o método descrito nos dados extraídos condiz com o resumo. O achado principal de 64% de identificação correta é amparado pelo percentual de 63,7% reportado, configurando suporte total.

items.title: Training human super-recognizers' detection and discrimination of AI-generated faces

judge.evidence_empirical: In two different experimental designs, we found that SRs (total N = 283) were better at detecting and discriminating synthetic faces than controls (total N = 381)
judge.evidence_topic: Here, we investigate synthetic face detection and discrimination in super-recognizers (SRs; who have exceptional face recognition skills), and typical-ability control participants.
judge.reason: O achado extraído reproduz exatamente o que diz o resumo: SRs foram melhores e controles sem treino ficaram abaixo do acaso.

items.title: AI Images vs. Real Photographs: Investigating Visual Recognition and Perception

judge.evidence_empirical: The visual perception of selected images was studied by means of eye tracking and gaze patterns as well as time characteristics, compared with consideration to the respondent groups' gender and knowledge of AI graphics.
judge.evidence_topic: The study assessed how people perceive 12 pictures generated by AI vs. 12 real photographs.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda a percepção de imagens geradas por IA, enquadrando-se no tema. É um estudo empírico com rastreamento ocular e participantes humanos. O tipo de estudo e método extraídos conferem com o resumo. O achado sobre imagens de animais de estimação e arquitetura ser mais fáceis de identificar é exatamente o relatado no resumo.

items.title: People are poorly equipped to detect AI-powered voice clones

judge.evidence_empirical: Through a series of perceptual studies, we report on the realism of AI-generated voices in terms of identity matching and naturalness. We find human participants cannot consistently identify recordings of AI-generated voices.

judge.reason: O artigo investiga a percepção de deepfakes em diferentes modalidades (vídeo, áudio) por participantes humanos, alinhando-se exatamente ao tema e recorte metodológico do pedido. O desenho experimental, com atribuição aleatória, configura estudo empírico com dados próprios. O achado extraído é fiel ao resumo.

items.title: Real and Deepfake Face Recognition: An EEG Study on Cognitive and Emotive Implications

judge.evidence_empirical: Electroencephalographic (EEG) data were collected from 23 healthy participants using a 21-channel dry-EEG headset; power spectrum and event-related potential (ERP) analyses were performed.
judge.evidence_topic: The prevalence of deepfakes, AI-generated images, poses challenges in discerning real from synthetic identities. This study investigated healthy individuals' cognitive and emotional engagement in a visual discrimination task involving real and deepfake human faces expressing positive, negative, or neutral emotions.
judge.reason: Article directly investigates human perception/discrimination of deepfake faces using EEG, matching request criteria; empirical with own data; method matches abstract; main finding is clearly stated in abstract.

items.title: AI-generated images of familiar faces are indistinguishable from real photographs

judge.evidence_empirical: Here, we investigated a new method for generating face images (via ChatGPT plus DALL·E) and its application to both fictional and real (in this case, celebrity) identities. Our results demonstrated that generated images of both fictional (Experiment 1) and celebrity identities (Experiment 2) could not be distinguished from real photographs.
judge.evidence_topic: generated images of both fictional (Experiment 1) and celebrity identities (Experiment 2) could not be distinguished from real photographs.
judge.reason: O resumo afirma diretamente que imagens geradas de identidades fictícias e de celebridades não puderam ser distinguidas de fotografias reais por observadores humanos, confirmando o achado principal.

items.title: Too beautiful to be fake: Attractive faces are less likely to be judged as artificially generated

judge.evidence_empirical: 150 participants rated 109 pictures of faces on 4 characteristics (attractiveness, beauty, trustworthiness, familiarity). The stimuli were then presented again with the new information that some of them were AI-generated, and participants had to rate each image according to whether they believed them to be real or fake.
judge.evidence_topic: Technological advances render the distinction between artificial (e.g., computer-generated faces) and real stimuli increasingly difficult, yet the factors driving our beliefs regarding the nature of ambiguous stimuli remain largely unknown.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga como pessoas julgam a autenticidade de rostos gerados por IA versus reais, com experimento empírico em humanos. O método descrito confere com o resumo, e o achado sobre o papel da atratividade com efeito de gênero está sustentado pelo resumo.
